  "anomaly_detected": true,
  "confidence": 0.6,
  "anomalies": [
    {
      "category": "open_connection",
      "components": ["D17", "D43", "D49"],
      "pins": ["D17.2", "D43.2", "D49.2"],
      "nets": ["/NET0185"],
      "observed": "The anodes of three LEDs (green D17, green D43, yellow D49) sit on net /NET0185 and nothing else. That net has no supply, resistor or driver. Their cathodes go through current-limit resistors to the Ethernet/PI status lines (NET0138, NET0033, NET0116), so these LEDs have no supply reference and cannot light.",
      "expected": "Status LED anodes should return to a supply rail (+3V3), as the other indicator LEDs on this board do (for example D15 and D35 have anodes on +3V3, and D26 is fed from +3V3 through R91).",
      "evidence": [
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(net (code \"42\") (name \"/NET0185\") (class \"Default\") (node (ref \"D17\") (pin \"2\") (pinfunction \"A\") (pintype \"passive\")) (node (ref \"D43\") (pin \"2\") (pinfunction \"A\") (pintype \"passive\")) (node (ref \"D49\") (pin \"2\") (pinfunction \"A\") (pintype \"passive\")))"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(net (code \"98\") (name \"Net-(D17-K)\")"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(node (ref \"D15\") (pin \"2\") (pinfunction \"A\") (pintype \"passive\"))"}
      ],
      "impact": "Three indicator LEDs (Ethernet/PI activity status) never illuminate, so the status indication is lost. The rest of the circuit is unaffected.",
      "confidence": 0.55
    },
    {
      "category": "wrong_value",
      "components": ["R40"],
      "pins": ["R40.1", "R40.2"],
      "nets": ["VOUTN", "VOUTP"],
      "observed": "R40 is valued \"24k\", but its description, footprint text and MPN all describe a 24 ohm part (\"24Ω 0805\", MPN FRC0805J240TSD). The value and the part identity disagree by three orders of magnitude.",
      "expected": "The value field should match the selected 24 Ω part (or the MPN and description should be corrected to 24 kΩ). Its role across the VOUTP/VOUTN rails should be confirmed against the intended resistance.",
      "evidence": [
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(comp (ref \"R40\") (value \"24k\") (footprint \"Resistor_SMD:R_0805_2012Metric\")"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(description \" 125mW Thick Film Resistors 150V ±100ppm/℃ ±5% 24Ω 0805 Chip Resistor - Surface Mount ROHS\")"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(field (name \"MPN\") \"FRC0805J240TSD\")"}
      ],
      "impact": "If the 24 Ω part is fabricated, the bleed/load across the high-voltage charge-pump outputs is about 1000 times lower than the value field suggests, which would load the outputs heavily and dissipate significant power. If 24 kΩ was intended, the wrong part was ordered.",
      "confidence": 0.4
    },
    {
      "category": "other",
      "components": ["U1", "U49"],
      "pins": ["U1.5", "U49.5"],
      "nets": ["GND"],
      "observed": "The GND2 (isolated-side ground) pins of both CAN isolation transceivers are tied to the main board GND net, the same as GND1. The isolated CAN side therefore shares the system ground.",
      "expected": "A galvanically isolated CAN transceiver should have its GND2 on a separate isolated ground, as the specification describes isolated CAN buses.",
      "evidence": [
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(node (ref \"U1\") (pin \"5\") (pinfunction \"GND2\") (pintype \"power_in\"))"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(node (ref \"U49\") (pin \"5\") (pinfunction \"GND2\") (pintype \"power_in\"))"},
        {"source": "spec", "quote": "two isolated CAN buses (`CAN0`, `CAN1`), each driven by its own MCP2515 SPI CAN controller ... through an isolated CAN transceiver"}
      ],
      "impact": "The isolation barrier is bypassed, so ground differences and transients on the CAN bus reach the controller ground. This may be a pre-existing design choice rather than a fault.",
      "confidence": 0.2
    }
  ],
  "summary": "The strongest deviation is three LED anodes (D17, D43, D49) left on a net with no supply connection, so those indicators cannot light. R40 is also valued 24k while its description and MPN specify a 24 Ω part. The isolated-CAN GND2 tie to system ground is a lower-confidence observation."
}

anomalies.observed: The anodes of three LEDs (green D17, green D43, yellow D49) sit on net /NET0185 and nothing else. That net has no supply, resistor or driver. Their cathodes go through current-limit resistors to the Ethernet/PI status lines (NET0138, NET0033, NET0116), so these LEDs have no supply reference and cannot light.
anomalies.expected: Status LED anodes should return to a supply rail (+3V3), as the other indicator LEDs on this board do (for example D15 and D35 have anodes on +3V3, and D26 is fed from +3V3 through R91).
anomalies.impact: Three indicator LEDs (Ethernet/PI activity status) never illuminate, so the status indication is lost. The rest of the circuit is unaffected.

anomalies.observed: R40 is valued "24k", but its description, footprint text and MPN all describe a 24 ohm part ("24Ω 0805", MPN FRC0805J240TSD). The value and the part identity disagree by three orders of magnitude.
anomalies.expected: The value field should match the selected 24 Ω part (or the MPN and description should be corrected to 24 kΩ). Its role across the VOUTP/VOUTN rails should be confirmed against the intended resistance.

evidence.quote: (description " 125mW Thick Film Resistors 150V ±100ppm/℃ ±5% 24Ω 0805 Chip Resistor - Surface Mount ROHS")

anomalies.impact: If the 24 Ω part is fabricated, the bleed/load across the high-voltage charge-pump outputs is about 1000 times lower than the value field suggests, which would load the outputs heavily and dissipate significant power. If 24 kΩ was intended, the wrong part was ordered.

anomalies.observed: The GND2 (isolated-side ground) pins of both CAN isolation transceivers are tied to the main board GND net, the same as GND1. The isolated CAN side therefore shares the system ground.
anomalies.expected: A galvanically isolated CAN transceiver should have its GND2 on a separate isolated ground, as the specification describes isolated CAN buses.

evidence.quote: two isolated CAN buses (`CAN0`, `CAN1`), each driven by its own MCP2515 SPI CAN controller ... through an isolated CAN transceiver

anomalies.impact: The isolation barrier is bypassed, so ground differences and transients on the CAN bus reach the controller ground. This may be a pre-existing design choice rather than a fault.
